uncited: Domain-Specific Adaptations extend 3D Gaussian Splatting to non-photometric domains by replacing view-dependent RGB color with scalar attributes or specialized geometric intersections [1875-volumetric-gaussian-splatting-avis.md], [3301-gaussian-splatting-for-microscopy.md], [5170-ultragauss-rendering.md].

Unlike standard 3D Gaussian Splatting which optimizes for novel-view synthesis from calibrated RGB images, these methods optimize against 3D volume data, microscopy stacks, or ultrasound probe planes using domain-specific loss functions and rendering primitives [1875-volumetric-gaussian-splatting-avis.md], [3301-gaussian-splatting-for-microscopy.md], [5170-ultragauss-rendering.md].

All adaptations retain the core 3D Gaussian primitive representation: a set of $M$ anisotropic 3D Gaussian kernels $\mathcal{G} = \{G_i\}_{i=1}^M$ [Application-Specific Extensions](13465-application-specific-extensions.md).

In radiative and domain-specific variants, this is replaced by view-independent scalar attributes or feature vectors [1875-volumetric-gaussian-splatting-avis.md], [3301-gaussian-splatting-for-microscopy.md], [5170-ultragauss-rendering.md].
